SQR2.title: Can the black king catch this pawn? #shorts
SQR2.desc:
The rule of the square. Black to move: draw a square from the pawn to the last row. If the king can step into the square, he catches the pawn. If he can't, the pawn gets away. Here 1...Ke5 steps in and wins the pawn; with the king on g5 he is one file too far and the pawn queens.

Did you know this rule?

#chess #endgame #chesstips

OPP2.title: White is a pawn up. Win or draw? #shorts
OPP2.desc:
The opposition: white king e5, pawn e4, black king e7. With Black to move, the black king has to step aside and the pawn queens: 1...Kd7 2.Kf6 Ke8 3.e5 Kf8 4.e6 Ke8 5.e7 Kd7 6.Kf7 and 7.e8=Q. With White to move, the black king keeps blocking the pawn and it ends in stalemate. Same position, and only the turn decides. Both lines checked with an endgame tablebase.

Would you have known?

#chess #endgame #opposition

FSH2.title: Should White take this knight? #shorts
FSH2.desc:
The Fishing Pole: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O Ng4 5.h3 h5. If White takes the knight with 6.hxg4, the h-file opens: 6...hxg4 7.Ne1 Qh4 8.f3 g3, and mate on h2 can no longer be stopped. So no, leave the knight alone: it is the bait.

Would you have taken it?

#chess #chesstraps #chessopenings

CST2.title: Your rook is attacked. Can you still castle? #shorts
CST2.desc:
Yes. Castling only looks at the king: no castling out of check, through an attacked square or into check. The rook may be attacked, and on the queenside it may even cross an attacked square (b1 or b8). A king that was checked earlier but never moved can still castle.

Did you know all of these?

#chess #chessrules #castling

WMIL.title: He left his queen hanging, then the windmill started #shorts
WMIL.desc:
Carlos Torre vs Emanuel Lasker, Moscow 1925: 25.Bf6!! Qxh5 26.Rxg7+ Kh8 27.Rxf7+ Kg8 28.Rg7+ Kh8 29.Rxb7+ Kg8 30.Rg7+ Kh8 31.Rg5+ Kh7 32.Rxh5, and Torre went on to win. The rook and the bishop take turns giving check: a windmill.

Did you know this game?

#chess #windmill #chesshistory
